tagline.text: A 2,404 m dormant volcano and ASEAN Heritage Park with a sacred Subanen crater lake

location.label: Location
location.text: Around Don Victoriano Chiongbian, Misamis Occidental (near Oroquieta and Ozamiz)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ozamiz Airport (OZC) or Laguindingan Airport (CGY) near Cagayan de Oro

children.text: Mount Malindang Range Natural Park is a forest protected area of about 53,000 hectares centered on the highest peak in Misamis Occidental (2,404 m), and it became an ASEAN Heritage Park in 2011. It is a quiet trekking destination with Lake Duminagat, a crater lake sacred to the indigenous Subanen people, plus waterfalls, hot springs and rare wildlife such as the Philippine eagle.
Mount Malindang is a complex volcano in Misamis Occidental in northwestern Mindanao, standing about

above sea level. It is the highest point in the province, and PHIVOLCS classifies it as inactive. No historical eruption is firmly confirmed; only an unofficial account places one around 1822 (some sources say 1819). Records show that a party led by Major E.A. Mearns made the first recorded ascent in May 1906.

The park around the mountain, Mount Malindang Range Natural Park, was declared a national park in 1971, reclassified as a natural park in 2002, and gained protected-area status by law (RA 9304) in 2004. It became an ASEAN Heritage Park in 2011. Figures vary slightly by source, but the area is about 53,000 hectares, divided into a core zone of about 34,000 hectares and a buffer zone of about 18,000 hectares. The park extends beyond Misamis Occidental into Zamboanga del Sur and Zamboanga del Norte.
The best-known spot for travelers is the crater lake
Lake Duminagat

, about 8 hectares in size. The indigenous Subanen people of the area believe it is home to the spirits of their ancestors, so fishing is prohibited, and stories say its water has healing powers. The park is also described as holding about 15 waterfalls and 3 hot springs, and Piduan Falls in Don Victoriano is often mentioned as a neighboring attraction.

It is ecologically valuable too. Management data record 1,284 plant species, 36 mammals, 162 birds, 33 reptiles and 26 amphibians, with the Philippine eagle, Philippine tarsier and Mindanao warty pig among the notable animals. The streams that begin on this mountain are also an important source of drinking and irrigation water for nearby cities and residents. With so few facilities, it is better seen as a place for quiet trekking and local village experiences than as a polished tourist site. First-timers are advised to do just the lake trip. A long summit trek needs fitness, gear and permit preparation, and because there are no facilities it is best attempted by experienced hikers with a guide. It is not widely known and so is rarely crowded, which makes it good for quiet walking.

This lake of about 8 hectares lies in cool forest at roughly 1,240–1,560 m above sea level (4,068–5,118 ft depending on the source). Few people visit, so it is very peaceful. Because it is a Subanen sacred site, visit quietly and do not fish or swim in the lake.
The most used route climbs past the Lake Duminagat camp to the north peak and is generally said to take
3 days, 2 nights
. The route has steep sections and frequent fog, so a guide is essential.
As you climb, farmland gives way to mossy forest. You can see rare plants such as ferns, orchids and pitcher plants, and roots and soil are slippery after rain, so take care.

With 162 bird species recorded, the lower forest is good for spotting endemic birds early in the morning. Animals such as the Philippine eagle and tarsier are elusive and hard to see, so count yourself lucky if you do.

There are about 15 waterfalls and 3 sulfur hot springs in and around the park. Piduan Falls in Don Victoriano is often combined with a lake visit in one day. Trails near the falls are slippery in the rainy season, so get local guidance.

Subanen communities, the original inhabitants of the area, live on the mountain's lower slopes. News reports have told the story of a family that served as the lake's unofficial caretakers. Ask permission before visiting or taking photos, and keep noise down.

The park was declared an ASEAN Heritage Park in 2011, recognizing its conservation value, and the Protected Area Management Board (PAMB) and local governments are pursuing ecotourism development. A road to the lake has also been discussed, so how you reach it may change in the future.
Take a bus or van from Ozamiz City to Don Victoriano. It is described as about
1–2 hours
from Ozamiz, depending on road conditions.
In central Don Victoriano, stop at the park office or the local government tourism office to confirm your permit and guide, and pay any entrance fee.
Take a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) to the trailhead. A full day including a guide is said to cost about
; confirm the final price locally before you go.
Hike from the trailhead up to the lake. It is generally said to take
1–2 hours
, and longer after rain.
Have lunch by the lake and look around quietly. Do not fish or swim in the lake.
Head down before dark and return to Don Victoriano. If it is late, stay in town or go back to Ozamiz.
A day trip to the lake alone is said to be possible, but the travel time is long, so an early start is essential. Follow the park office's guidance on the schedule.

items.title: 3 nights 4 days summit challenge
items.subtitle: Via the Duminagat camp to the north peak

children.text: After confirming your permit and checking gear, climb from the trailhead to the Lake Duminagat camp. Camp at the designated site by the lake.
Climb the ridge from the lake camp toward the summit. There are steep, foggy sections, so the guide must lead the way.
Explore the summit area, then head toward the descent.
Come down to the trailhead and return to Don Victoriano or Ozamiz.
The summit route is usually described as
3 days, 2 nights
, but the number of days varies by source. Ask the park management office for the exact schedule and permit conditions.
Whether flights run from Manila to Ozamiz Airport (OZC, also called Labo Airport) changes with the season, so check the latest schedule.
A more common option is to fly from Manila to Laguindingan Airport (CGY) near Cagayan de Oro, then continue overland to Ozamiz by bus or van. Travel time depends on traffic, so confirm locally.
A bus or van from Ozamiz City to Don Victoriano is described as taking about
1–2 hours
Another route, described on blogs, is to take a bus from Ozamiz toward Molave (Zamboanga del Sur) and transfer, but confirm this locally.

Oroquieta City and Ozamiz City are the base towns, and Ozamiz is said to have better bus and ferry links, restaurants and ATMs. There are other entry points too, such as Calamba, Lopez Jaena and Sapang Dalaga.
From Don Victoriano to the trailhead, a habal-habal is the usual way. A full-day fare including a guide is said to be about
Roads are rough with unpaved stretches, so access can be difficult in the rainy season.
Many guides say the dry season from January to May is when trails are driest and best for walking. March to May is especially recommended, with lowlands around
by day and the summit area around

From June to November, frequent showers bring mud, leeches and swollen streams. Rain can still fall on some days outside those months, so always check the forecast and park office notices before departing.

There is almost no lodging or restaurant at the designated camps by the lake, so bring your own tent, sleeping bag, food and water purification. Villages near the trailhead have only small sari-sari stores, so it is best to shop in advance in Ozamiz or Don Victoriano.

It is easier to find lodging in Ozamiz City or Oroquieta City. Ozamiz is the city best equipped with a bus terminal, restaurants and ATMs. Camping requires park office approval, so discuss your lodging plans with the office first.

Village meals are often simple, such as rice with grilled fish or chicken. The day before the trek, stop at the local market in Ozamiz to stock up on fruit, bread, canned food and energy bars, and bring a plastic bag to carry your trash back. Even if you purify stream water, it is safer to boil it or use a filter.
Contact the park management office (PAMO) in advance to get a visit permit. Reports say it asks for your itinerary, a list of participants and ID copies.
A guide is required for safety. It is safer to arrange one through the local government tourism office.
Pack a waterproof jacket, trekking shoes, spare socks, a headlamp and plenty of water. In the rainy season, leech socks also help.
Bring plenty of cash. There are almost no ATMs in the villages below the mountain.
Respect the Subanen sacred site. Fishing and noise at the lake are prohibited, and ask permission before taking photos.
Mobile signal is weak in many stretches, so tell your lodging or guide when you expect to return.
Roads in the park and the way to the lake may change with development plans, so check the latest notices before you leave.
If you are coming from Manila or Cebu, travel can take a full day, so it is safer to stay the first night in Ozamiz and start early the next morning.
This is a protected area that requires a visit permit and a guide. Fees and permitted sections differ by source, so be sure to check the latest guidance with the park office.
Fog and sudden showers on the mountain make it easy to get lost. Do not go without a guide.
Streams can rise quickly after rain, so do not cross them; turn back instead.
Do not chase or feed wildlife, and do not pick plants or fruit.
Carry out all your trash, and do not use soap or detergent near the lake.
Security and safety conditions change over time, so check with local authorities and your government's travel advisory before departing.

A major city close to Laguindingan Airport. It is the gateway for the overland route toward Ozamiz.
